Find the volume of the solid region above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front and right ones, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117154/assets/7c1738e97bc16a32f86d6901136afc4d9e288035d170fcd640db340ad36d19c5.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z},
$$

where $D$ is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane.

To find the top boundary curve of $D$ in the form $z=z(y),$ we substitute $x=1$ into the equation $x=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z:$

$$
1=2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z\,⟹\,z=2-\frac{2}{3}y
$$

Then, we have

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117154/assets/ea8b8397163309a11aa478fcc21ab53ee293c19f0d77a93b5c3d3472bb0eba70.png)

Hence, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2-\frac{2}{3}y,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{1}{3}y-\frac{1}{2}z}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3-z/2}dx\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2-y/3-z/2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}(2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2})-0\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-2y/3}2-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{z}{2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[(2-\frac{y}{3})z-\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2-2y/3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}((2-\frac{y}{3})(2-\frac{2y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}{(2-\frac{2y}{3})}^{2})-0\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})((2-\frac{y}{3})-\frac{1}{4}(2-\frac{2y}{3}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(2-\frac{2y}{3})(\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{6})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}3-\frac{4y}{3}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}\,dy \\  & ={[3y-\frac{2{y}^{2}}{3}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{27}]}_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =(3(3)-\frac{2(3)^{2}}{3}+\frac{{3}^{3}}{27})-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
